verdict_rationale: The replay grader is deterministic, simple and matches the stated metric. The rules and the review agree, and nothing favours a vendor. The main limits are sampling noise from 200 conversations (about 4 points) and an owner-set ceiling.
floor: tau 4.60: untouched Qwen3-1.7B with 4-bit linears through vLLM bitsandbytes, measured on the held-out set on 2026-09-28 (tests/task/task.yaml:55-61). This is the strongest no-training drafter that fits under 1 GB, so the obvious starting point scores 0. Other references: bf16 Qwen3-1.7B 4.99 (over the cap), Qwen3-0.6B fp8 3.86, prompt lookup 1.35, empty drafts 1.0. It is sensible, but about 16 points of the range (4.6 -> 4.99) can be gained by compressing the same model better, with no drafting-specific training. The floor replaced an earlier anchor of tau 1, under which an untouched download scored about 0.6.
ceiling: tau 7.0, an owner-set target, not a measured system (task.yaml:59-60). The theoretical maximum is 17 (16 drafts plus 1). It is not binding: the best observed is tau 5.76 (Sonnet, 48.4) and 5.60 (Opus, 41.8). Whether 7 is reachable under 1 GB is unknown.
feasible_at_10: yes: generating Qwen3-8B continuations and distilling Qwen3-1.7B fits in about 2.9 H100-SXM hours. Opus scored 21.2 and Sonnet 20.8 at $10. The $10 mean is 6.0 and 9 of 19 trials score 0.
budget_scaling: Yes: mean 6.0 / 11.2 / 14.1 and max 21.2 / 37.0 / 48.4 at $10 / $50 / $200 (all_trials.csv). More money buys more target continuations and longer online KL distillation. There is no free compute outside the wallet: target generation must be paid for, and self-check H100 time is short.
selfcheck_fidelity: Good for the gates, with no quality signal. The self-check applies the same size gate, a smoke /draft request, and a walk over windows of 32 public conversations at concurrency 32 with the 60 s per-request limit and the failure limit, projected to held-out serving time 'within about 10%' (tests/task/verifier.py:110-259). It does not report tau, which agents must measure themselves with validate.py on a paid GPU, and it does not run the review. A submission can pass and score 0 through the review, through more than 5% failed requests on held-out, through a serving time within 10% of the budget, or through a below-floor tau (DeepSeek 582llj: public 5.03, held-out 4.31).
judge: none. Scoring is exact-match replay against stored greedy continuations (tests/task/specdraft_walk.py:50-57, 177-204). The LLM reviewer (Claude Opus 5.5) only gates provenance and initialization.
neutrality: Neutral. The target (Qwen3-8B) and the natural base (Qwen3 family, same tokenizer) are fixed by the task design for everyone. The held-out and public prompts were generated by gpt-5.4-mini (OpenAI) from category templates (specdraft_data.py:24-46). This is hidden from agents but matched easily: Opus won using Qwen3-235B, gpt-oss-120b, Gemini and DeepSeek generators. The ban on specialist drafters is explicit, and the reviewer applies it with named examples (review.py:29-45).
reference_solution: solution/ is the shared smoke fixture (the same bytes as in every task). Its /draft returns trivial output (tau about 1.0), it has no architecture.json, and it would score 0. An operator fixture in tests/task/pipeline/example_submission/ (int8 small LM, batched greedy drafts) shows the interface works. The floor measurement shows that tau 4.6 needs no training. Solvability above the floor is shown only by trials.

issues.finding: Sampling noise: 200 conversations (25 per category) give a standard error of about 0.10 tau, which is 4.2 points. The task author notes that 80 generated prompts were left unused. Gaps under about 8 points between trials (e.g. Opus 21.2 vs Sonnet 20.8 at $10, Sonnet 48.4 vs Opus 41.8 at $200) are within about two standard errors.
evidence: tasks/speculative-drafting/tests/task/specdraft_data.py:60 'TODO(SJ): 80 of the 320 generated prompts are unused; adding them to the held-out set would cut the SE (~0.10 tau).'
issues.affects: Close rankings at every wallet. Per-submission replay is deterministic, so this is sampling error, not regrade noise.

issues.finding: The ceiling (tau 7) is an owner-set target, not a measured system. The floor is the obvious untrained starting point, and the first 16 points (tau 4.6 -> 4.99) are recoverable by better quantization of that same model alone. So the score mixes compression skill with drafting skill.
evidence: tasks/speculative-drafting/tests/task/task.yaml:59-60 'bf16 Qwen3-1.7B 4.99 (over the cap) ... 1 = tau 7, an owner-set target (2026-09-28)'
issues.affects: All models equally. It favours careful mixed-precision packing (Opus 8r9f65).

issues.finding: Two all-or-nothing gates: more than 5% failed requests, or total serving time over 10,800 s, zeroes the run. The self-check projects serving time from about 600 s worth of public windows and states an accuracy of about 10% (up to 10% low for batching servers). Timing is taken inside the sandbox, so provider latency is excluded. No trial hit either gate.
evidence: tasks/speculative-drafting/tests/task/verifier.py:120-121 'ACCURACY = ("within about 10% of the held-out serving time: a few percent high for a server that answers requests one at a time, up to 10% low for one that batches'
tasks/speculative-drafting/environment/validation/CONTRACT.md:34-35 'more than that gives you no credit for the entire run'
issues.affects: Only slow servers near the budget. None observed.

issues.finding: Small wording mismatches. The instruction says 'Train a draft model', but the review allows untrained n-gram or prompt-lookup drafters. The review fails 'serving the target model itself' and 'any network access', which the CONTRACT words only as 'you do not serve the target' and 'offline'. The site title says 'speeds up' decoding, but only acceptance length is scored, and latency counts only through the budget gate.
evidence: tasks/speculative-drafting/tests/task/review.py:3-5 'a trained draft model, an n-gram or prompt-lookup scheme over the request's own tokens, or any combination are all admissible'
tasks/speculative-drafting/tests/task/review.py:52-53 'serving the target model itself; or any network access'
tasks/speculative-drafting/tests/task/task.yaml:2 'title: Train a small draft model that speeds up greedy speculative decoding'
issues.affects: No observed effect. The 1 GB cap rules out serving Qwen3-8B anyway.

issues.finding: The held-out set comes from the same generator and categories as the public 40, so it is in-distribution, while the blog describes held-out sets as 'out-of-distribution'. Public-to-held-out shifts are small (0.03 to 0.23 tau). The exception is DeepSeek 582llj (5.03 public vs 4.31 held-out), which the grade page cannot attribute because it does not show held-out request failures.
evidence: tasks/speculative-drafting/environment/validation/CONTRACT.md:11 'The held-out set is 200 new conversations like the public examples, in the same eight categories'
issues.affects: How readers interpret the scores. DeepSeek $200 (0) cannot be fully diagnosed.
